chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated from Ja'far, from Al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Hanan, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'May Allah bless the one who is easy in selling, easy in buying, easy in paying debt, and easy in collecting debt.'

key_terms.سَهْلِ الاِقْتِضَاءِ: Easy in collecting debt (lenient when demanding what is owed)
key_terms.سَهْلِ الشِّرَاءِ: Easy in buying (being lenient when purchasing)
key_terms.سَهْلِ الْبَيْعِ: Easy in selling (being lenient in price or terms)
key_terms.سَهْلِ الْقَضَاءِ: Easy in paying debt (prompt and generous repayment)

ai.seo_question: What are the four commercial behaviors that Allah blesses according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on trade ethics, this hadith highlights the Prophetic tradition of facilitating commerce through leniency (*sahl*) rather than rigidity. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on moral conduct in economic dealings, where ease in buying, selling, debt repayment, and collection is viewed as a divine blessing that fosters social harmony and financial justice.
